title: Engel wins Moscow Race 2 after an early stop and a safety car
dek: Maro Engel won DTM Race 2 at Moscow Raceway from 17th on the grid, 0.376 seconds ahead of Mattias Ekström, after a first-lap stop and a safety car reshuffled the order.

chapters.title: Audi’s Saturday, and the weights still in the paddock
text: Saturday had belonged to Audi. René Rast inherited pole from the penalised Marco Wittmann, led from start to finish and beat Mike Rockenfeller, racing on a broken foot, by 0.770 seconds. The win put Rast back at the top of the championship on 99 points, four ahead of Lucas Auer and six ahead of Mattias Ekström, who had finished eighth after an opening-lap clash with Timo Glock. Wittmann recovered from sixth on the grid to take third.

Sunday brought the same ballast picture: Mercedes carried 10 kg more than Audi and 5 kg more than BMW, even after Audi’s one-two. Robert Wickens, fourth, had been the best of the Mercedes drivers in Race 1. As on Saturday, the race was scheduled for 55 minutes and included one mandatory tyre-change stop.

chapters.title: Blomqvist is fastest, then disqualified
text: Rockenfeller set an early reference of 1:27.886 in the 20-minute session before Gary Paffett and then Wickens moved the best time to 1:27.230. Rast went top with 1:27.153, only for Ekström to better it with a 1:26.934, the quickest lap of the weekend so far. The cars went back to the pits at the halfway point, and the order was settled in the final attack. Paul di Resta put his Mercedes top with 1:26.887, before Rast and then Bruno Spengler beat it; Spengler’s 1:26.579 set the bar.

Tom Blomqvist then found more. His 1:26.518 was the fastest lap of the weekend and put the second Team RBM BMW on pole. The pole lasted for less than two hours. The stewards disqualified Blomqvist from qualifying because his car did not have enough fuel left in the tank to draw the required sample, and he was sent to the back of the grid.

The pole therefore went to Spengler, 0.003 seconds ahead of Ekström, who started alongside him. Rast and di Resta, the best Mercedes, took the second row. The bonus points for the top three in qualifying went to Spengler (3), Ekström (2) and Rast (1). Jamie Green was moved back five places for a third warning of the season and started 15th. Auer was 12th and Rockenfeller, second a day earlier, 14th. Maro Engel lined up 17th, with only Blomqvist behind him.

chapters.title: Four drivers stop after one lap and the safety car follows
text: Spengler held the lead into the first corner from Ekström, with di Resta passing Rast for third. Behind them, Maxime Martin and Loïc Duval touched at the start, and Duval was warned. Wittmann, Duval, Engel and Blomqvist took an aggressive tyre strategy: all four made their mandatory stop at the end of the first lap, and Wittmann called it a plan that had worked well until Nico Müller got in the way.

On lap six the safety car came out. Martin, who had been caught up in the first-corner contact, lost his brakes and stopped at the side of the track with the brakes on fire; he picked up an extinguisher himself. Wittmann and the early stoppers were suddenly well placed, since the field was bunched up behind the safety car for three laps. The restart brought no changes among the front-runners, and Spengler stayed ahead of Ekström and di Resta.

chapters.title: Müller holds the field up while Engel waits
text: Ekström passed Spengler at the final corner around lap 11 and pulled away. Spengler stopped from second place around lap 15 and fell to the middle of the field, Ekström a lap or two later. As the leaders pitted, di Resta briefly inherited the lead and then Paffett, who had yet to stop, took over, with Green, Edoardo Mortara and Müller running behind him on their original tyres. Wittmann, stopped since lap one, was the virtual leader of the race.

Engel passed Wittmann on the main straight and, once Green made his stop around lap 24, sat directly behind the leader Müller, who still had his stop to make. Müller, on worn tyres, kept the queue behind him. With about ten minutes left, Engel, Wittmann, Duval and Blomqvist were running second to fifth behind him, and Ekström, who had already stopped, had time to close up from the middle of the field.

chapters.title: Engel holds off Ekström by 0.376 seconds
text: Müller made his stop with about three minutes remaining, and Engel took the lead. Ekström, on fresher tyres, passed Blomqvist and Duval and then went after Wittmann, who was running second. He got by in the final minute or so and set off after Engel, but the laps ran out. Engel, who had to look after his tyres and was not sure how many laps were left, crossed the line 0.376 seconds ahead for his first DTM victory, in his 52nd race.

Spengler had fought back after his stop and finished third, 3.981 seconds behind the winner. Rast was fourth, Green fifth and Wittmann, who had been on course for a podium, dropped to sixth. Blomqvist, who had started last after losing his pole, finished seventh, ahead of Auer, Wickens and Mortara in the top ten.

chapters.title: Ekström leads Rast by one point as the weights row boils over
text: Engel called the final stint the longest five or six laps of his life and said he had not realised how close the race was to its end when Ekström appeared in his mirrors. Mercedes team principal Ulrich Fritz admitted the team had been lucky with the safety car, but said Engel had stayed cool and brought the win home.

Ekström said he would have needed one more lap to pass Engel, having lost too much time behind Wittmann, and described the race as wild and almost hardcore. Audi’s head of motorsport Dieter Gass called it an incredible race with everything in it. Rockenfeller, who had crossed the line seventh, was given a five-second penalty for using DRS on too many laps and was classified 12th. For BMW, Spengler said the safety car had been unlucky and that, under normal conditions, the team would not have had a chance of winning, but he was happy with the podium. BMW’s motorsport director Jens Marquardt said his drivers had fought to the end, while RMG team principal Stefan Reinhold was disappointed by the tactical games after a weekend of incidents.

The result changed the championship again. Ekström’s second place and his qualifying points put him back in front on 113 points, one ahead of Rast on 112, with Auer third. Rast, who had won on Saturday and finished fourth on Sunday, slipped one point behind.

The performance weights meanwhile overshadowed the sport. German motor sport federation president Hans-Joachim Stuck said that a solution that abolished the weights must be found, and announced he would call the manufacturers, the ITR and the federation together immediately after the Moscow race. ITR chief Gerhard Berger said he had been saying since the first race that the weights had to go, and called them too expensive to justify. The DTM then took a four-week summer break, with the sixth round at Zandvoort on 19–20 August.

facts.t: Engel’s first DTM win in his 52nd race
facts.v: Maro Engel won from 17th on the grid, 0.376 seconds ahead of Mattias Ekström, after stopping for tyres at the end of the first lap.
